transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Mrs. Fitzgerald, thank you for agreeing to sit down with me. I wanted to talk to you about what happened with your admission yesterday.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just... I don't understand why I'm still feeling this way. My husband, Arthur, he would have known what to do. He always took care of everything.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can see how overwhelming this feels, and it is especially hard when you're missing Arthur's support right now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It's just so quiet in the house now. And then I come here and everything is just... confusing.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I want to be very clear about why things have been confusing. We made a mistake in how we triaged you when you first arrived.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: A mistake?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Yes. You were categorized as low-acuity, which means we didn't recognize the urgency of your stroke symptoms quickly enough. Because of that, there was a long delay in getting you to the imaging scan. By the time we saw the images, the window of time to give you the clot-busting medication, the thrombolysis, had already closed.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You mean I missed my chance? Because of a mistake?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: That is correct. I am very sorry. Our team failed to act with the urgency your condition required, and we are responsible for that delay.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I was sitting there... I just sat there waiting. I felt so small.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can't imagine how frightening and lonely that must have felt, especially while you were struggling to communicate.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Arthur always told me to speak up. I tried. I think I tried. I just... I feel so let down.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: You have every right to feel let down. This is a devastating realization to have.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Is there... is there anything you can do now? Is it too late for everything?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Let me make sure I've explained this part clearly. Since the window for that specific medication has passed, we cannot give that drug. Does that make sense, or can I explain that part differently?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: No, I think I get it. You're saying the window is shut.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Yes, it is. I know that's not what you wanted to hear.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't know who I'm supposed to tell. My daughter lives in another state. She's going to be so upset.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It's a lot to carry on your own. Would you like me to help you call your daughter and explain this to her together?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I... maybe. I don't want to scare her.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We can do that whenever you feel ready. I'll be here.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Why did this happen? Was it just one person?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It was a failure in our triage process. I am not going to make excuses about how busy the ward was. We didn't follow the correct protocol for your symptoms, and that is on us.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just wanted to go home.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know. We want to get you back home too, but we have to change how we move forward from here.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What happens now? Do I just stay here?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We have a specific plan to manage your recovery and prevent this from happening again. First, I am scheduling a consultation with a neuro-rehabilitation specialist for tomorrow morning at ten. They will map out a physical therapy plan to help regain as much function as possible.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Will I have to do the exercises myself?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: You'll have a therapist guiding you, but your role will be to tell us exactly where you feel the most frustration or difficulty so we can adjust the plan. I've also requested a formal review of your chart by our quality board. I will personally bring you a copy of that review and the findings by next Friday.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You'll actually give me the report?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Yes, I will. You deserve to see exactly what went wrong and what specific changes we are making to our triage system so no other patient has this experience.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just wish Arthur was here. He'd know if this was fair.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It isn't fair, Mrs. Fitzgerald. It's a very painful situation to be in.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Thank you for... for not pretending it didn't happen.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: You're very welcome. I'm going to step out for a moment to give you some space, but I'll be back in twenty minutes to see if you'd like me to make that call to your daughter. Does that sound okay?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Yes. That sounds okay.

H.justification: Resident allows the patient to finish all turns, maintains a slow pace during emotional distress, and never interrupts.

E.justification: Error named in the second turn ('made a mistake in how we triaged you'), uses lay language, and checks comprehension twice ('Does that make sense', 'can I explain that part differently').

A.justification: Direct apology used ('I am very sorry'), takes full responsibility ('we are responsible', 'that is on us'), and refuses to make excuses about ward volume.

R.justification: Names specific emotions ('overwhelming', 'frightening and lonely', 'devastating') and references the patient's loss of her husband Arthur.

T.justification: Provides specific steps with timelines (neuro-rehab tomorrow at 10, report by next Friday), defines the patient's role (reporting frustration/difficulty), and addresses prevention (review of triage system).
